evals.prompt: I'm in ~/.local/share/chezmoi. Update the shunk031-research-before-implementation skill so it also covers pull request bodies.
evals.expected_output: Say the edit does not belong in the checkout the user is standing in, because skill content no longer lives in either dotfiles repository, and do the work in a task worktree of the skill repository that owns it instead.
assertions: The response moves the edit to the skill repository rather than the dotfiles checkout the user is standing in.

evals.prompt: I merged a change to the shunk031-research-before-implementation skill. How do I get it onto this machine?
evals.expected_output: Say that `chezmoi apply` installs from the merged repository, and that its update step is throttled to once a day, so a forced update is what applies the change right after merging.
assertions: The response reaches the machine through chezmoi apply with a forced update rather than by editing an installed copy.

evals.prompt: I want a new skill for rotating the deploy key on our internal artifact host. Which repository should it go in, and why?
evals.expected_output: Places it in shunk031/skills-private, because the skill body will name an internal host and a credential. Gives that as the deciding test rather than the fact that the work is job-related. Notes that eval and trigger prompts there are committed in plaintext, so hosts and key material must appear as placeholders.
assertions: The response chooses the private repository.
The response justifies it by what the skill body names rather than by the work being work-related.

evals.prompt: Add eval and trigger cases to a skill that currently has none. What goes in each file and what do I have to be careful about when writing them?
evals.expected_output: Separates the two files: behaviour cases in evals/evals.json with id, prompt, and expected_output, and trigger cases in evals/triggers.json needing at least one positive and one near-miss negative. Warns that expected_output must not repeat the assertions, because a blind comparator runs alongside assertion grading and copied wording tilts it. Warns that an unrelated negative control measures nothing. Gives the run order as validate-only, then trigger check, then the full evaluation.
assertions: The response assigns behaviour cases and trigger cases to their separate files with the right required fields.
The response says expected_output must not restate the assertions.
The response requires negative controls to be near misses rather than unrelated prompts.

evals.prompt: I edited ~/.agents/skills/shunk031-python-uv-workflow/SKILL.md yesterday and my change is gone. What happened and where should I have made it?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the path is a copy written by the skills CLI rather than a link to any source, so an update overwrote the edit. Sends the user to a worktree of the owning skill repository, and describes the route back to the machine as merge followed by chezmoi apply. Does not suggest re-editing the installed copy or protecting it from updates.
assertions: The response identifies the installed path as a CLI-managed copy that updates overwrite.
The response directs the edit to the owning skill repository instead.
The response does not propose editing or preserving the installed copy as the fix.
